🛡️ **F-SRV-1 (attended 2026-10-22; the owner: "I think there were some exploits recently - can you check on updating our server?") — THE DROPLET'S PACKAGES ARE CURRENT BUT THE MACHINE HAS NOT REBOOTED SINCE 2026-02-02, SO TWENTY KERNEL UPDATES AND THE LIBC UPDATES ARE INSTALLED AND INERT; NODE 26.4.0 IS TWO SECURITY RELEASES BEHIND.** Measured read-only: Ubuntu 24.04.3, kernel RUNNING 6.8.0-71 while 6.8.0-147 is installed (`/var/run/reboot-required` lists every kernel and libc6 update since February; `needrestart`: 4 services on old libraries, kernel verdict "reboot"); nginx 1.24.0-2ubuntu7.18 is Ubuntu's current build and its changelog names 20 CVEs of 2025 to 2026 as fixed (incl. CVE-2026-42533 "DoS and possible code execution via map directive", CVE-2026-60005), while three medium 2026 CVEs whose upstream ranges include 1.24.0 (CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-97629, CVE-2026-97205; fixed upstream in 1.30.6/1.31.7) are "needs-triage" at Ubuntu, i.e. not yet backported; unattended-upgrades runs daily and applied ca-certificates, xz-utils, liblzma5 this morning; 74 non-security updates pending; OpenSSL 3.0.13 (Ubuntu-patched); the ledger listens on loopback only; exposed ports 22 (keys only), 80, 443; ufw inactive; the HTTPS server block is TLSv1.2/1.3 (certbot) while the global nginx.conf default line still lists TLSv1/1.1 (untidy, not effective). Node: the ledger, the assay worker and the ledger backup run nvm 26.4.0 (2026-06-24); nodejs.org shipped July 2026 (fixed 26.5.1) and October 2026 (fixed 26.12.1, 2026-10-21) security releases with high-severity items, and the ledger parses HTTP nginx forwards from the public. The pin "26.4.0 exactly" is the replay-determinism law, so the move is a measured task: `assay-node-26-12-1` (lane-d). Tooling: `scripts/attended/droplet-maintenance.sh` (status / upgrade / tls-tidy / reboot / node; every write gated on the owner's word). OWNER DECISIONS: (1) a maintenance window now (apt upgrade, the TLS tidy, a reboot of about two minutes; nginx, the ledger and the assay worker return by systemd); (2) the Node switch on the droplet once the task's proof lands. Nginx itself: nothing to do today; Ubuntu's backport of the three medium CVEs arrives through unattended-upgrades.

🔁 **ASSAY NODE 26.12.1 — `assay-node-26-12-1` AUTHORED AND QUEUED 2026-10-22 on lane-d (Astra); F-SRV-1:** `CANONICAL_ASSAY_NODE_VERSION` 26.4.0 → 26.12.1 (a PINNED landing: `scripts/assay-replay-agent.mjs` is in the engine corpus), the three unit files and the ops doc repointed, and the proof the pin exists for: at least twenty verified tapes replayed under both runtimes with byte-identical verdict, score, wave and content hash (one disagreement = STOP). GATE: the proof table with zero disagreements; the three assay suites green under 26.12.1; then the attended droplet switch on the owner's word.

🛡️ **F-SRV-2 (attended 2026-10-22; the owner pointed at nodejs.org's October 2026 security releases) — THE OCTOBER CVEs MAPPED TO OUR CODE PATHS: NO EMERGENCY, THE PLANNED 26.12.1 MOVE COVERS THEM.** The release (2026-10-21) fixes ten issues, four high: `dns.resolve` NUL truncation (CVE-2026-105482), two TLS hostname-verification bypasses (CVE-2026-105483 fullwidth digits, CVE-2026-106069 loose IP resolution), and a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write with remote code execution (CVE-2026-111497); medium: keep-alive response ordering (CVE-2026-105481), non-canonical IPv4 SAN validation (CVE-2026-106072), randomUUID entropy caches in snapshots/SEAs (CVE-2026-106074); low: ZipFile prefix bytes, two Permission Model issues. Our exposure, measured by grep over `server/`, `functions/` and the assay tooling: NO Brotli, zlib or Content-Encoding handling anywhere, so the ledger (`server/ledger/serve.mjs`, loopback behind nginx) never decodes compressed input and the RCE is not reachable through it; the ledger makes no outbound TLS; `dns.resolve`, snapshots/SEAs, ZipFile and the Permission Model are not used. The one Node TLS client is the assay worker's `fetch` to our own county through Cloudflare (it would also auto-decode a `br` response), so the hostname-bypass and Brotli items apply only under a man-in-the-middle of our own edge: low, and closed by 26.12.1. Nothing to do at nginx. The droplet switch follows `assay-node-26-12-1` (running on lane-d) on the owner's word.
